### T-047 — `test/blong-ci-report` reserves Playwright ports nothing uses yet

> _2026-09-15 · ci · open_

`test/blong-ci-report` is registered as the 45th project in `rush.json`, which reserves CI ports
9045/9145 for it. Playwright ports are derived from each package's index in the `projects` array,
and nothing uses Playwright in that package yet, so the ports are only reserved. Reorder that array
only with the port derivation in mind.

### T-092 — The prose validator never checks verdict completeness

> _2026-09-15 · skills · open_

analyze-prose.ts validateFindings validates every verdict it receives (known segmentId, known
category, verbatim quote) but never checks that each segment of the chunk received one, although the
prose-anomaly prompt demands an entry for EVERY segment id and session-analyser.ts claims 'no silent
failures'. A model that omits a segment therefore passes unnoticed. The log-embed-prd run reported 0
findings, 0 rejected and 7640 explicit normal verdicts for 7641 segments — only that one-segment
arithmetic gap exposed the omission; a parseable reply with several omissions would look identical
to a clean session. Detect it by comparing chunk.segments.length against findings + normalVerdicts +
rejected and surfacing the shortfall in the coverage block.

### T-093 — The stacked metrics pull request must be merged by hand

> _2026-09-16 · ci · open_

The stacked pull request is deliberately not auto-merged: workflows are left off for the stacked
branch for now (a stacked pull request may not spend a CI run on two generated files), so nothing
can merge it and enabling auto-merge would first mean deciding what is allowed to run for a
metrics-only change. Until then the baseline reaches main only when a human merges the stacked pull
request; an unmerged one is rebuilt on every run and the same pull request is refreshed, so nothing
is lost.

### T-124 — Give manifest artefacts a compare-only command for docs check

> _2026-09-22 · docs · open_

blong-dev docs check is side-effect-free for artefacts whose generator only writes the registered
destination, but not for the two produced by Playwright specs: writing their markdown needs
--update-snapshots, which also rewrites that package's committed _.play.ts-snapshots baselines, and
check does not snapshot or restore those. So a full docs check can leave modified baselines. Both
artefacts are already guarded by their own packages (ci-ui runs the same spec, which compares the
artefact and fails when it is stale), so the workaround is to run check filtered to flows._ and
png.\*. The proper fix is a second, compare-only command per artefact in
docs/blong/docs-artifacts.json. Recorded as item 5 in the Further considerations of
plans/docs/VISUAL_DOCS_PLAN.md.

### T-126 — The ACL matrix cannot show a seeded wildcard rule

> _2026-09-22 · docs · open_

VERIFIED, not a guess. aclMatrixRows in realm/blong-access/adapter/db/accessModel.ts:645 filters
.where('ab.targetKind','scope'), and its own comment says only scope rules are returned because
scope rules are the ones the matrix writes. The shared seed stores its wildcard as target: '\*' in
realm/blong-access/meta/db/accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml, which the merge writes as targetKind
'all', a different storage from the sentinel-scope row the matrix uses for the same '(all records)'
label. Consequently the Admin role shows 15 wildcard allows in the ACL Rules page and in its Access
tab, while every cell of its Record Access matrix is empty: a reader of the matrix cannot see or
narrow a wildcard that a seed granted. The seed and the matrix need to agree on one representation,
or the matrix needs to render 'all' rules as read-only cells. Related, smaller: the access.acl
browse search does not match the Principal column, so searching Admin returns no rows although the
column reads Admin, and the only way to pin those rows from the UI is a column filter.

### T-054 — A missing `report-src` degrades CI quietly with only a warning

> _2026-08-21 · ci · open_

A missing `report-src` only produces a `::warning:: report source not found` in `deploy-report`, so
a regression in the `reports` artifact upload degrades quietly - `include-hidden-files: true` is
what keeps `.ci-report` in that artifact. The links inside the report are likewise _predicted_ from
the reports base URL rather than collected from the publish jobs, so a failed publish leaves a dead
link behind a report that still reads as complete. The predicted set now includes each Playwright
trace, both the summary row's viewer link and the one written into the Allure results by
`linkTraces` (D-316), so that risk covers the trace URLs as well. Consider failing the publish job
instead, once the hidden-file fix has proven itself in CI.

### T-178 — blong-access as a library realm is untested, and blong-party is not one

> _2026-09-29 · cross-cutting · open_

core and access are declared library realms (D-324), but only core's arrangement has been exercised:
access is a library realm because it can supply access control to services that run off their own
database, and that case has no test or example yet. The complication to work out is blong-party,
which is deliberately not a library realm because it holds business data that must not be copied per
database, yet an access realm in such a database may hold triples that point at party resources
living elsewhere. A triple names ids rather than rows, so the reference itself is cheap; what is
missing is a worked-out answer for a realm that is a library in one database and a client of a
non-library realm in another — whether the graph reference is resolvable at all, and what the
failure looks like when it is not.

### T-191 — The Hindsight image tag is floating, so a pull can change the bank

> _2026-10-01 · cross-cutting · open_

plans/memory-index/hindsight.sh starts ghcr.io/vectorize-io/hindsight:latest, and --pull always
means an update can change the server under a bank whose volume cannot be re-embedded: the vector
width is fixed by the first write. The bank config was read back on 2026-10-01 with
retain_extraction_mode chunks, enable_reranking true and the built-in BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, and
that is the configuration the committed script now applies. Record the server version the settings
were verified against and consider pinning an image digest, so a later run can tell whether the
store changed under it.

### T-062 — Backend state is ephemeral for minio, redis, kafka and vault

> _2026-09-10 · cross-cutting · open_

The `minio`, `redis`, `kafka` and `vault` backends have no `volumeMounts` or `persistentVolumeClaim`
in their `test/integration/*.yaml` manifests — unlike mysql, mongodb and keycloak, which have PVCs.
Any cluster restart therefore wipes their data silently while the corresponding one-shot init Jobs
stay `Complete`, so they never re-seed.

Mitigated locally: `~/.local/bin/k3d-up` now deletes all init Jobs, re-applies `test/integration/`,
waits for them and ensures the `blong-<suite>-<user>` MySQL databases, so a host restart self-heals.
Every init Job is idempotent as of that change. CI is unaffected because it always starts a fresh
k3d cluster. Remaining candidates, not implemented: add a PVC to `minio-deployment.yaml` /
`kafka-deployment.yaml` so restarts preserve the data outright; or make the s3 test create its own
bucket, which was rejected for now because the `commander/hello.txt` object is intentionally
provisioned by k8s so that Playwright screenshots stay deterministic.

Kafka no longer needs the PVC for its _seed_: the deployment's `lifecycle.postStart` hook now runs
the same message-guarded seed as the Job, so the container restart that recreates the topic re-seeds
it too (D-498). A PVC would still be the only way to keep the messages themselves across a restart,
and minio, redis and vault remain as recorded here.

### T-342 — Decide the cache payload shape before landing step 2

> _2026-10-14 · ci · done_

Step 2 of the CI cache plan waits on a choice that run 38593732609 turned into a real decision
rather than a mechanical one, and it is the user's to make. The archive holds 208 877 files and its
save costs 41m22s, while a local `tar` plus `zstd` of the same tree takes 2.8s, a restore of that
same 767 MB takes 20s in six jobs and the 271 MB Playwright archive saves in 6s — so the price is
per enumerated file, about 12 ms each, and the `build / audit` job pays the same rate for 20m40s
through the `**/audit/auditResults.json` glob of its `Upload Audit Results` step. Narrowing
`CACHE_PATHS` to the store plus `*/dist` and `*/.rush` therefore takes 208 877 files to 85 358 and
still leaves roughly seventeen minutes of save, which is why the choice matters. The options are to
pack the store into a single `deps.tar.zst` and cache that one file, which keeps the warm cache the
user asked for and turns the save into an upload measured in seconds; to pack and narrow the list at
the same time; to narrow alone; or to drop the pnpm cache and have every job install from the npm
registry in parallel. The recommendation is to pack, in both `rush.yaml` and `release-docker.yaml`
because the two share one key and have to agree on the payload, and to fix the audit glob in the
same change, since it is twenty minutes of billed runner time per run for one small file. Nothing of
step 2 is written yet: the diagnosis is F-522, the strategy is D-545 and D-546, and the
implementation is one edit to `CACHE_PATHS` plus a pack step and an unpack step.

Decided and implemented: the store travels as one deps.tar.zst, the derived trees leave the payload,
and the audit job gates on a ci-audit script with its glob narrowed. Both workflow files updated in
infitx-org/actions, awaiting push.

### T-355 — Build blong-dev ci, the publisher fix and the blong-ci skill

> _2026-10-16 · ci · done_

The work agreed on 2026-10-16 after the run 622 analysis, in the order it is worth doing.

First the publisher, because it makes everything after it cheap: `failures.json` gains a `message`,
a `location`, a trimmed evidence excerpt and the `leg` for each failure, and a package whose non-tap
leg failed is published as failed rather than passed. That closes @@T-352 and is what turns the
ordinary diagnosis into a single HTTP request.

Then `blong-dev ci` under `tools/blong-dev/src/ci/`: target resolution (an open release-please PR to
its head sha to the run that built it), a client for the reports site (`failures/<workflow>/<n>/`,
the per-package pages for a previous run's verdict and duration), a `gh api` wrapper for jobs, job
logs and artifacts, selective artifact extraction that keeps only the failing packages' `.ci-report`
files, and a raw-tap reason parser that reports the failing `not ok`, `expired:`, the last `ok`
before it, the `at.fileName/lineNumber/source` tap already prints, the per-test `# time=` and the
coverage ERROR lines that are consequences rather than causes. Classification compares the package
with its previous published run; the artifact is cached under gitignored `dev/ci/<run>/`. Register
it in `cli.ts` and `usage.ts`.

Target resolution has to skip runs that published nothing — in progress, cancelled (run 623 was
cancelled on 2026-10-16 and published nothing), or green, since a green run publishes no failure
bundle at all — and fall back to the newest run that does have a report, saying which run it used
and why the newer ones were passed over. `failures/<workflow>/latest/failures.json` is the stable
alias for that run and is what the test leans on: it still resolves to run 622 and the same two
packages, which is the truth the explicit `--run 622` variant asserts.

Then `.github/skills/blong-ci/SKILL.md` following the frontmatter template in
`.github/skills/_shared/conventions.md`: the default target rule, one command first, the
interpretation table (tap `timeout!` and `expired:` mean the file budget expired, in-file
`setTimeout` overrides the runner's `--timeout=240` per @@D-247, coverage errors are consequences, a
streaming story's image snapshot is timing-dependent, a package has several legs and only some write
the report), the us-or-the-runner comparison rule, and the output contract.

The files are tested with unit fixtures for the parser and the site client and with an acceptance
test that uses run 622 as ground truth (three failed operations, the leg gap, two timeouts and one
snapshot) and run 621 as its "was green" counterpart.

Finally the path is validated with a fresh-context subagent, which is the only test of the thing
that was actually wrong: it took 35 tool calls to answer "check the failure in the last build". The
subagent is given no context beyond the sentence a user would type —
`check the failure in the last build of blong` — with no mention of the skill, the command, the run
number or this plan, because the question is whether the skill's description routes an agent to it
and whether the tool answers in one call. The verdict is judged against the known truth of run 622
plus whatever run the agent resolved for itself: three failing operations including the storybook
leg the bundle used to omit, the blong-cli file budget expiring after four of its five tests,
kukum's gateway test stalling inside `kukum.source.check`, and the FilteredServer image snapshot
that only differs because the story streams on a timer. Pass means at most four tool calls and two
turns against that 35-call baseline, the skill loaded, `blong-dev ci failures` the first thing
reached for, and a verdict that names the budget and the file setting it instead of calling a loaded
runner a regression. Every call the agent had to make that the tool should have made is a tool gap
and every step it improvised is a skill gap, and each becomes a friction or a todo entry rather than
a note in the chat. Two variants follow the main run: an explicit `--pr 200` for the non-default
target path, and a green run for the no-failure path, which must not invent one. Run it twice with a
fresh subagent each time, since one sample of routing proves nothing, and refresh the skill index
(`blong-dev memory index --semantic --sources skill`) first so the skill is findable by meaning and
not only by name. The default prompt and the explicit one ask different questions: the explicit
`--run 622` variant must land on 622, while the default one must land on the newest run that has a
report and say so — when that run is green, the same prompt becomes the no-failure case.

(tapExcerpt.ts) and a non-tap leg publishes its own slice; blong-dev ci is a command group
(failures, runs, history) with the release-please PR as its default target and --full for the
artifact; .github/skills/blong-ci/SKILL.md documents the interpretation; the fixture is run 622 with
